title: SocGen Raises S&P 500 Target Again - TradingView
text: SocGen Raises S&P 500 Target Again Less than 1 min read SPX The S&P 500 (SPY) could climb to 8,000 by the end of 2026 as AI-driven earnings growth offsets concerns about rich valuations, according to Societe Generale, according to Seeking Alpha. The bank raised its year-end target to 8,000 from 7,300, arguing that AI will drive earnings while the Federal Reserve determines how much investors are willing to pay for them. SocGen's base case assumes about $375 in S&P 500 earnings per share and a forward PE multiple near 21 times. A more dovish Fed and faster AI monetization could push the index toward 10,000, while tighter policy could pull it closer to 6,000. SocGen said its stance remains bullish, not blind. The bank noted that forward 12-month earnings growth has accelerated to about 18%, while earnings have begun to outpace share price gains, helping to stabilize valuations. SocGen said the rally is no longer just a Magnificent Seven story, with equal-weight indexes and small caps improving. The next thing to watch is whether AI earnings keep rising fast enough to absorb Fed and valuation risk.
